narrative.overview:
Kitchen OS should feel like the notebook that lives by the fridge: warm paper, a short list of what to do today, and honest notes about what's in stock. The mood is warm, calm and honest. Nothing shouts. Urgency is carried by four functional status colours and plain words, never by alarm styling. Density is moderate. The app is used one-handed, often with wet hands and at arm's length, so controls are sturdy and forgiving, and type stays generous.

The world is warm near-white paper (Rice Paper) with one deep herb green (Pandan) for action and one warm orange (Kalabasa) for anything you need to buy. A soft serif (Fraunces) sets titles; a neutral sans (Inter) carries everything you read as data or tap. Light and dark are one token swap; components never branch on theme.

The home screen direction approved on 2026-10-25 takes two quiet cues from JRPG menus: a double-ruled card for the one thing that matters most today, and a freshness bar that shows how much life an ingredient has left. The influence stays in form and never reaches the words (see Do's and Don'ts). Evidence: the private design canvas linked in PLAN.md 5.5.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper surfaces, hairline borders and a soft, slightly lifted shadow.
One action colour (Pandan) and one buying colour (Kalabasa); four status colours that only ever mean expiry.
Serif titles, sans everything else, tabular numbers for quantities.
44px minimum targets; primary actions in the thumb zone.
Every status shown as a word first, with colour and graphics as support.

rules.name: The Status Words Rule
rules.body: The four status colours mean one thing: how soon food expires (and, by extension, have / not enough). Never use them for branding, categories or decoration, and never show one without its word.

rules.name: The Three Roles Rule
rules.body: Text uses the -fg role, tints use -bg and -border, and the base value is for dots, bars and fills only. A base status colour is never used as text.

rules.name: The Kalabasa Is For Buying Rule
rules.body: Orange marks what you need to get. Never white text on Kalabasa or on status amber; use the soft tint with its ink.

rules.name: The Serif Titles Rule
rules.body: Fraunces sets titles only: page titles, section headings, sheet and empty-state titles, and the wordmark. Anything a person taps, scans or compares is Inter.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Quantities, counts and dates use tabular figures (.tabular), so columns and counters don't jitter.

rules.name: The Paper On A Counter Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces get a hairline and the Card shadow. Only things that float (sheets, dialogs, toasts, the floating action button) and an interactive card under the pointer take Pop.

rules.name: The Double-Rule Rule
rules.body: The double border marks the single most important card on a screen. Never more than one per screen, and never on list rows.

rules.name: The Label Carries It Rule
rules.body: A freshness bar never appears without its text label, and never shows a number. The bar is hidden from assistive tech, because the label beside it says the same thing.

dos: Do style through the Tailwind tokens (bg-brand, text-status-soon-fg), never raw hex in components, and join classes with cn().
Do show every status as its word first: Use now, Use soon, Fresh, Expired, No date, with "est." on every estimate.
Do keep every control at least 44px tall, and keep the main actions in the thumb zone on phones (the floating action button) and in the sidebar or page header on desktop.
Do use Fraunces for titles and Inter for everything else, with tabular figures for numbers.
Do honour reduced motion: remove motion that moves, but keep spinners and progress turning (.motion-keep).
donts: Don't use game vocabulary (HP, quest, KO, level, reward, party). The JRPG influence lives in form only, confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-25.
Don't use Faint for text people must read: it's 3.4:1 on white. It's for icons, chevrons and separator dots only; section labels, placeholders, hints and inactive tabs use Muted (PLAN 5.3).
Don't put a coloured stripe thicker than 1px down the side of a card or row. The old 4px status rail was replaced by the freshness bar in PLAN 5.8.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
Don't put white text on Kalabasa or status amber.
Don't use more than one double-ruled card on a screen.

Don't pin a button in place over scrolling content. Floating actions are sticky, like the Save bar: they float while there's more below and settle after the last content, so the end of a page is never covered (owner, 2026-10-25).
